verdict_reason: _intra_sentence_mean_cosine reproduces Ethayarajh 2019's IntraSim -- mean cosine of each token vector to the SENTENCE-MEAN vector, not the pairwise token-token mean -- to rel <= 1e-10 against an independently written reference, over 20 random (2..30) x 16 clouds. Definitions 1-2 are exactly invariant under a positive common rescale and the implementation now is: unchanged to rel 1e-9 at 1e-30, 1e-8, 1e8, 1e25 and 2.406159650500376e38, the regime where a plain np.linalg.norm underflows because it squares before summing.
comparable_reason: No comparability defect established. An earlier draft of this verdict cited a 4.37% order sensitivity in mean_anisotropy_baseline; that was measured at num_samples=20 while this task SHIPS num_samples=1000, fifty times larger. A sampling-noise figure taken 50x below the shipped configuration is not evidence about the shipped configuration, and re-measuring at N=1000 was not completed here, so the claim is WITHDRAWN rather than restated with a caveat.
github_reason: The released analyze.py averages token-to-sentence-mean similarities for IntraSim; that definition was reimplemented independently and matches to 1e-10.
paper_reason: Ethayarajh 2019 reports SelfSim/IntraSim for BERT/ELMo/GPT-2 on its own corpus; not reproducible under this task's corpus protocol without adopting that corpus.
confounds_reason: None established. The anisotropy baseline is estimated from the same corpus, which is worth attention in principle, but no measurement at or near the shipped num_samples=1000 was made in this pass.
fix: No implementation change required on the evidence gathered. OPEN: order sensitivity of the anisotropy baseline at the shipped num_samples=1000 was not measured; the only figure obtained (4.37%) is at N=20 and is not attributable to the shipped protocol.
